Hi, thanks for your report.

Sorry for unmerging your issue from another similar one, but we're struggling to reproduce the issue you're showing in your video clip. To help us with debugging, please consider uploading an avatar with this setup on it and then sharing the ID of that avatar here. The avatar doesn't need to be public, and you don't need to worry about setting up animator controls to move the capsule sender around - we can move it manually.

To clarify, proximity is intended to be calculated from the nearest point inside the sender to the receiver's positive Z face as the docs describe. So while your video does seem to show proximity behaving in the wrong way, the expected value would be the right edge of the capsule, not its center point. This is the intended behavior and probably won't change - if you need the middle of the shape specifically, you could consider reducing the capsule's radius instead.
In fairness, the documentation could be clearer about this point. We'll get the docs updated to be more specific.

@{65f4b1a3d0a7a0c657a7d3a8|full_name} Hello! No worries, I'm happy my report is being looked at.

I figured some more stuff out while looking at it again. This is quite embarrassing but it turns out I completely forgot about the curves in the animation clip so that's where the inaccuracy was coming from in the original video clip and since the proximity is supposed to calculate from the edge then there is not really a bug here, everything tested in the clip works as intended.

I made this test setup when I realized my contact tracker with 3 box receivers doesn't work as well as the version with 6 spheres. That one is actually super inaccurate for me. Depending on the angle of a capsule sender, it positions the receiver very differently and I’m fairly sure I did everything correctly this time. I attached a video clip showing off the inaccuracy but from my understanding, that is a different issue (the one I got merged with) that is already being fixed?

Sphere ID: avtr_97a770e7-f6eb-4590-8dc7-ba6faba50bf7

Box ID: avtr_3a43fb8b-cc92-42f9-bfd8-abd25e2e07a2

As for the proximity stuff, I now see that I should have filed this under a feature request rather than a bug report. I do agree with the current implementation and I think it's correct, I'm not asking to change that. It would still be nice to have an option of calculating from the center of a sender as this would make it work more predictably with differently sized fingers on avatars for things like a touch screens, possibly even the contact tracker could work better with that setup.

Thanks for checking out my report, sorry for the trouble!

@{67a7a794c9467977e8b07090|full_name} Thanks very much for doing some extra research, very appreciated!

After checking your avatar samples, unfortunately the behavior of your box avatar seems to be the same both with and without the change that solves this other issue: https://feedback.vrchat.com/bug-reports/p/contact-receiver-box-with-face-proximity-calculate-the-incorrect-distance

I can see the box avatar is essentially detecting fingers (all capsule senders) inside three large box contacts that completely surround the player, so I wouldn't expect that to be caused by the issue referenced in the other report above which is specifically when you have a capsule that goes through a box completely without stopping in it.

It might be useful to have a minimal repro case that just demonstrates the part of the contact system that you feel is failing, since it's difficult to tell what you're expecting to happen from your video. Assuming you're expecting the green marker to stay on the inside of the blue sphere, this might be because of differences in how proximity is calculated compared to what you're expecting (edge vs center)?

Thanks for the added context around proximity calculation. Exposing more info about proximity contacts is a popular existing feature request, and we are currently considering ways of achieving that.

@{65f4b1a3d0a7a0c657a7d3a8|full_name} Hello!

Thanks for reviewing my report and the testing. I see now that the video didn't highlight what to look for. (With box contacts, the small trackers drift away from the fingers depending on orientation, with spheres they are locked in almost perfectly)

What I was hoping to do is to reduce the contact amount per finger from 6 (X+, X-, Y+, Y-, Z+, Z-), to just 3: (X, Y, Z). This would reduce the necessary contact count on my prefab from 24 to 12. I did some more testing, as I suspected earlier, my inaccuracy issue comes from the proximity being calculated from the nearest contact point, rather than the center of the receiver.

-With spheres, when the sphere is in the center of the contact, the value is always reported as 1.0

-With box contacts, the value when the Z FACE is in the center of the sender is reported as 1.0 (correct). However when the box itself is in the center of the sender, it gets reported as 0.515 (depending on the size of the sender) instead of 0.5 (which is what I expected)

This is all intended and correct. Unfortunately without a way to calculate proximity from the center of a contact sender, box receivers can't be used in this case for the purpose of optimization. I will have to stick to the 24 contacts for now.

If possible, as you mentioned earlier, I would love for the decision to not expose X Y Z distance: https://feedback.vrchat.com/avatar-30/p/expose-more-information-to-contact-parameters-resulting-in-massive-contact-reduc

be revisited. Exposing more information would allow me and many other developers to reduce the complexity of our prefabs. (I could turn my 24 contacts into just 2!)

In any case, I really appreciate you looking into this! Sorry for the time waster, there isn't really a bug here, just a feature request and feedback. Next time I will take more time to check everything before making a report!

Setup from the video available here (just in case)

https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Qu5KUS9EgYuP8YcXjV0Y214Qhcm_da61/view?usp=sharing

@{67a7a794c9467977e8b07090|full_name} That all makes sense, thanks very much for taking the time to investigate further and explain what you're looking for. We're still internally discussing how to handle the feature request you've linked to. I will close your report here for now as the system is currently working the way it should, but I would also recommend that you vote for the report you've linked to if you haven't already and watch it for updates, since that's where we're most likely to make further announcements about this issue. Apologies if this is disappointing, we are aware of the desire for more info from contacts and are looking for ways to get there.

details:
I am trying to create a touch screen of sorts using the new box contacts.

Unfortunately with the current system, the "Face Proximity" seems to calculate the distance from the Z face to the closest point in of the sender instead of its center. This makes it impossible to use in this case as scaling a capsule contact will change what value the face proximity will report, even if it stays in the same position

Additionally, there seems to be some sort of a smoothing curve applied to the end result which makes the reported value very inaccurate.

These options make sense for most contacts, but face proximity should not force this behavior. There should be an option to calculate the distance of from the senders center point to make the calculations scale-agnostic and not use the smoothing curve for accuracy.

SDK Version 3.10.4
title: Box Contact "Face Proximity" is scale dependent and very inaccurate
